answer: At a wharf trading basalt and marble, relay agents earn voting weight from measured bandwidth, not key count. Agents send distinct verifier-chosen random payloads to measuring servers during the same timed window; only bytes received before its deadline count. A thousand aliases sharing one uplink must divide its capacity; more weight needs more bandwidth. Count each transfer once. This limits free influence from extra keys, not common ownership: rented links buy power, colluding verifiers can fabricate traffic, and slower honest agents lose out.
